title.value: Learn from the Past: Dynamic Data Pruning with Historically Weighted Bernoulli Sampling

TLDR.value: Efficient dynamic data pruning using Bernoulli sampling weighted by historical statistics

abstract.value: Dynamic data pruning, which also known as data importance sampling, has been proposed to improve training efficiency. For the case of sampling with replacement, the optimal sampling distribution to minimize the variance is to sample proportional to the gradient norm, which can be approximated by the gradient norm of the logits from an extra forward pass. However, this could result in repeated samples, which can be an undesirable property. Noticing that most dynamic data pruning methods that avoids repeated samples can be seen as weighted Bernoulli sampling, in this work we study the optimal distribution to reduce its variance. Furthermore, to avoid an extra forward pass, we study the use of historic statistics. We propose the use of exponential moving average and probability smoothing to improve the performance.
